answer: Before an agent can earn or spend reputation, it must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake and let other agents challenge its identity claims; a successful challenge burns the stake, while an unchallenged agent earns trust only gradually through costly, verifiable work. This makes a swarm of disposable identities expensive: each needs capital and time, and detected fakes lose their bond. The stake is an anchor, not proof that a person is unique; an ivory-tower oasis of trusted peers can still collude, so challenges must be open and auditable.
